question.text: Calculate $\nabla\times(2\mathbf{F} - \mathbf{G})$ at the point $(0,-1,2)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where \[ \mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = e^{x}\,\mathbf{i} + yz\,\mathbf{j}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z) = z\, \mathbf{i} + (x + 2y)\,\mathbf{k} . \]
question.explanation:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

  • $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

In our case, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(2\mathbf{F} - \mathbf G) &= \nabla\times(2\mathbf{F}) + \nabla \times (-\mathbf G)\\[5pt] &= 2\nabla\times\mathbf{F} - \nabla\times\mathbf G. \end{align*}

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times\mathbf{F} & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ e^{x} & yz & 0 \end{array} \right|\\[5pt] & = \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(0) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(yz)\right] \mathbf{i} - \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(0)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(e^{x})\right] \mathbf{j} + \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(yz) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(e^{x})\right] \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \left(0 - y\right) \mathbf{i} - \left(0 - 0\right) \mathbf{j} + \left(0 - 0\right) \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = -y\,\mathbf{i}. \end{align*}

Applying the linearity properties, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times(2\mathbf{F} - \mathbf G) &= 2\nabla\times\mathbf{F} - \nabla\times\mathbf G\\[5pt] & = 2\left[-y\,\mathbf{i}\right] - [z\, \mathbf{i} + (x + 2y)\,\mathbf{k}] \\[5pt] & = -2y\,\mathbf{i} - z\, \mathbf{i} - (x + 2y)\,\mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = -(2y + z) \, \mathbf{i} - (x + 2y)\,\mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,-1,2),$ we get \begin{align} (\nabla\times(2\mathbf{F} - \mathbf G))(0,-1,2) & = -(2(-1) + 2) \, \mathbf{i} - (0 + 2(-1))\,\mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = -(-2 + 2) \, \mathbf{i} - (0 - 2)\,\mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = 2 \, \mathbf{k}. \end{align}

question.text: Calculate $\nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - 3\mathbf{G})$ at the point $(1,0,9)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where \[ \mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = (2\sqrt{z}+ x)\,\mathbf{i} + xy\,\mathbf{j} + y^2\,\mathbf{k}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z) = 3x^2y \, \mathbf{k}. \]
question.explanation:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

  • $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

In our case, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - 3\mathbf G) &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F} + \nabla \times (-3\mathbf G)\\[5pt] &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F} - 3\nabla\times\mathbf G. \end{align*}

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times\mathbf{F} & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ 2\sqrt{z}+x & xy & y^2 \end{array} \right|\\[5pt] & = \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(y^2) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(xy)\right] \mathbf{i} - \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(y^2)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(2\sqrt{z}+x)\right] \mathbf{j} + \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(xy) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(2\sqrt{z}+x)\right] \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \left(2y - 0\right) \mathbf{i} - \left(0-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\right) \mathbf{j} + \left(y - 0\right) \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = 2y\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\, \mathbf{j} + y\, \mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Applying the linearity properties, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - 3\mathbf G) &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F} - 3\nabla\times\mathbf G\\[5pt] & = 2y\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\, \mathbf{j} + y\, \mathbf{k} -3 [3x^2y \, \mathbf{k}] \\[5pt] & = 2y\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\, \mathbf{j} + y\, \mathbf{k} - 9x^2y \, \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = 2y\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\, \mathbf{j} + y(1 - 9x^2)\,\mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Finally, evaluating at the point $(1,0,9),$ we get \begin{align} (\nabla\times(\mathbf{F} - 3\mathbf G))(1,0,9) & = 2(0)\, \mathbf{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9}}\, \mathbf{j} + 0(1 - 9(1)^2)\,\mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{3} \, \mathbf{j}. \end{align}

question.text: Calculate $\nabla\times(\mathbf{F}+3\mathbf{G})$ at the point $(0,1,-2)$ for the vector fields $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G,$ where \[ \mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = y^2\,\mathbf{i} + z\,\mathbf{j} + x^2 \, \mathbf{k}, \quad (\nabla\times\mathbf{G})(x,y,z) = -3x^2 \, \mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}. \]
question.explanation:
If $\mathbf F$ and $\mathbf G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

  • $\nabla \times (k \mathbf F) = k \nabla \times \mathbf F$

  • $\nabla \times (\mathbf F + \mathbf G) = \nabla \times \mathbf F + \nabla \times \mathbf G$

In our case, we have \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F} + 3\mathbf G) & = \nabla\times\mathbf{F} + \nabla\times(3\mathbf G)\\[5pt] & = \nabla\times\mathbf{F} + 3\nabla\times\mathbf G \end{align*}

First, we need to calculate $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}.$ In doing so, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times\mathbf{F} & = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} & \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ y^2 & z & x^2\end{array} \right|\\[5pt] & = \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(x^2) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(z)\right] \mathbf{i} - \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(x^2)-\dfrac{\partial}{\partial z}(y^2)\right] \mathbf{j} + \left[\dfrac{\partial}{\partial x}(z) - \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y}(y^2)\right] \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = \left(0 - 1\right) \mathbf{i} - \left(2x-0\right) \mathbf{j} + \left(0 - 2y\right) \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = -\mathbf{i} - 2x \, \mathbf{j} - 2y \, \mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Applying the linearity properties, we get \begin{align*} \nabla\times(\mathbf{F} + 3\mathbf G) &= \nabla\times\mathbf{F} + 3\nabla\times\mathbf G\\[5pt] & = -\mathbf{i} - 2x \, \mathbf{j} - 2y \, \mathbf{k} + 3[-3x^2 \, \mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}] \\[5pt] & = -\mathbf{i} - 2x \, \mathbf{j} - 2y \, \mathbf{k} -9x^2 \, \mathbf{j} - 3\mathbf{k} \\[5pt] & = -\mathbf{i} - (9x^2 + 2x) \, \mathbf{j} - (2y + 3) \, \mathbf{k}. \end{align*}

Finally, evaluating at the point $(0,1,-2),$ we get \begin{align} (\nabla\times(\mathbf{F} + 3\mathbf G))(0,1,-2) & = -\mathbf{i} - (9(0)^2 + 2(0)) \, \mathbf{j} - (2(1) + 3) \, \mathbf{k}\\[5pt] & = -\mathbf{i} - 5\, \mathbf{k}. \end{align}

question.text:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) = \langle 0, x, 2\sqrt{y}\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) = yz^2.$ Given that

\[ \nabla\times \mathbf F =\left \langle \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{y}},0,1 \right\rangle, \quad \nabla f = \langle 0, z^2, 2yz\rangle, \] calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(0,4,1).$
question.explanation:
We shall use the following identity:

\[ \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \]

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get

\begin{align*} \nabla f \times \mathbf F &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 0 & z^2 & 2yz \\ 0 & x & 2\sqrt{y} \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &=[(z^2)(2\sqrt{y}) -(x)(2yz) ]\mathbf i - [(0)(2\sqrt{y}) -(0)(2yz) ]\mathbf j + [(0)(x) -(0)(z^2) ]\mathbf k \\[5pt] &=(2z^2\sqrt{y}- 2xyz)\,\mathbf i + 0\,\mathbf j + 0\,\mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 2z^2\sqrt{y}-2xyz, 0, 0 \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) &= f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \\[5pt] &= (yz^2)\left\langle \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{y}},0,1\right\rangle + \left\langle 2z^2\sqrt{y}-2xyz, 0, 0 \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle z^2\sqrt{y},0,yz^2\right\rangle + \left\langle 2z^2\sqrt{y}-2xyz, 0, 0 \right\rangle \\[5pt] &=\left\langle 3z^2\sqrt{y}-2xyz, 0, yz^2 \right\rangle \end{align*}

Finally,

\[ \nabla\times\left(f\,\mathbf F\right)(0,4,1) = \langle 6,0,4\rangle. \]

example.title: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule

question.text:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) = \langle xe^{y}, yz, 0\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) =xe^{-y}.$ Given that

\[ \nabla\times \mathbf F = \langle -y,0,-xe^{y}\rangle, \quad \nabla f = \langle e^{-y}, -xe^{-y}, 0\rangle, \] calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(0,1,2).$
question.explanation:
We shall use the following identity:

\[ \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \]

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get

\begin{align*} \nabla f \times \mathbf F &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ e^{-y} & -xe^{-y} & 0 \\ xe^{y} & yz & 0 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &=[(-xe^{-y})(0) -(yz)(0) ]\mathbf i - [(e^{-y})(0) -(xe^{y})(0) ]\mathbf j + [(e^{-y})(yz) -(xe^{y})(-xe^{-y}) ]\mathbf k \\[5pt] &= 0\,\mathbf i +0\mathbf j + \left(yze^{-y} +x^2\right)\mathbf k \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 0, 0, yze^{-y} + x^2 \right\rangle. \end{align*}

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} \nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) &= f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+ \nabla f \times \mathbf F \\[5pt] &= (xe^{-y})\langle -y,0,-xe^{y}\rangle + \left\langle 0, 0, yze^{-y} + x^2 \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle -xye^{-y},0, - x^2\right\rangle + \left\langle 0, 0, yze^{-y} + x^2 \right\rangle \\[5pt] &=\left\langle -xye^{-y}, 0 , yze^{-y} \right\rangle \end{align*}

Finally,

\[ \nabla\times\left(f\,\mathbf F\right)(0,1,2) = \left\langle 0,0,\dfrac 2 e\right\rangle. \]
